svg.title: Absolute and relative extrema, and what the Extreme Value Theorem needs
svg.desc: Left: f(x) = x cubed minus 3x on the closed interval from -1.8 to 2.3. Flat tangent lines mark a relative maximum at (-1, 2) and a relative minimum at (1, -2), which is also the absolute minimum. The absolute maximum, about 5.27, is at the right endpoint x = 2.3. Right: g(x) = x for 0 ≤ x < 2 with g(2) = 0. The graph climbs toward an open circle at (2, 2) but the value 2 is never reached, so g has no maximum value; g is not continuous at 2.
svg.text: Continuous on a closed interval: both extremes are reached
A jump at x = 2: no maximum value
